meta.title: AssayIndex Published Catalog
meta.disclaimer: AssayIndex is an informational reference workspace. Verify current requirements, ordering details, and billing guidance with the source laboratory before ordering or submitting claims.

assays.summary: HLA-B27 association testing helps support evaluation of spondyloarthropathies when interpreted alongside clinical findings.
assays.purpose: Support diagnostic workups for ankylosing spondylitis, reactive arthritis, and related rheumatologic presentations.

assays.summary: Quantitative BCR::ABL1 p210 assays are used for therapeutic monitoring and molecular response tracking in chronic myeloid leukemia.
assays.purpose: Monitor established p210-positive CML or Ph-positive ALL and trend treatment response over time.

assays.summary: Factor V Leiden testing evaluates the common inherited thrombophilia associated with activated protein C resistance and venous thromboembolism risk.
assays.purpose: Assess patients at risk for inherited thrombophilia when results may change counseling or management.

assays.summary: Thiopurine pharmacogenomic testing evaluates TPMT and, in some offerings, NUDT15 variants that influence thiopurine toxicity risk.
assays.purpose: Support thiopurine dosing and toxicity risk assessment before or during treatment with azathioprine, mercaptopurine, or thioguanine.

assays.summary: EGFR mutation analysis evaluates targetable and resistance-associated variants in non-small cell lung cancer specimens.
assays.purpose: Support targeted therapy selection and resistance assessment in NSCLC.

assays.summary: HIV-1 viral load assays detect and quantify HIV-1 RNA in plasma for clinical management and treatment monitoring.
assays.purpose: Establish baseline viral burden and monitor antiretroviral therapy response.

assays.summary: HFE variant analysis evaluates common hereditary hemochromatosis-associated variants such as C282Y, H63D, and S65C.
assays.purpose: Assess suspected hereditary iron overload syndromes and support genotype-informed interpretation with iron studies and clinical context.

assays.summary: BCR::ABL1 kinase domain mutation testing evaluates acquired variants associated with tyrosine kinase inhibitor resistance.
assays.purpose: Investigate suspected TKI resistance in BCR::ABL1-positive leukemias with rising or nonresponsive molecular disease burden.

assayLabRecords.handling: Send whole blood specimen in original tube. Do not aliquot.
assayLabRecords.useOrClinicalSignificance: Assists in the diagnostic process of ankylosing spondylitis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, and reactive arthritis.
assayLabRecords.collectionInstructions: Send whole blood specimen in original tube.
assayLabRecords.rejectionCriteria: All specimens will be evaluated at Mayo Clinic Laboratories for test suitability.
assayLabRecords.limitations: HLA-B27 is associated with several rheumatic diseases but is not diagnostic in isolation.
assayLabRecords.interferences: Extreme temperature changes during shipping may alter specimen acceptability.
assayLabRecords.notes: Useful-for and LOINC metadata sourced from Mayo Test Catalog overview.

assayLabRecords.storage: Maintain blood specimen at room temperature.
assayLabRecords.methodology: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) / sequence-specific oligonucleotide probes (SSOP)
assayLabRecords.useOrClinicalSignificance: Evaluate spondyloarthritis and other disorders associated with HLA-B27.
assayLabRecords.rejectionCriteria: Hemolysis; clotted specimen; tube other than lavender-top (EDTA) tube
assayLabRecords.limitations: A positive result supports but does not establish a diagnosis of ankylosing spondylitis or related disorders.
assayLabRecords.interferences: Adequate testing requires intact lymphocytes at the time of testing.
assayLabRecords.notes: Labcorp describes this as a class I antigen level test.

assayLabRecords.recordTitle: ARUP Quantitative Detection of BCR::ABL1, Major Form (p210)
assayLabRecords.testName: Quantitative Detection of BCR::ABL1, Major Form (p210)
assayLabRecords.specimenVolume: Whole blood: 5 mL; bone marrow: 3 mL
assayLabRecords.minimumVolume: Whole blood: 3 mL; bone marrow: 1 mL
assayLabRecords.handling: Refrigerate immediately. Separate specimens must be submitted when multiple tests are ordered.
assayLabRecords.stability: Must be received within 48 hours of collection due to RNA lability.
assayLabRecords.methodology: Reverse transcription PCR, quantitative monitoring assay
assayLabRecords.useOrClinicalSignificance: Appropriate for therapeutic monitoring of BCR::ABL1 major (p210) positive chronic myeloid leukemia or acute lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma.
assayLabRecords.collectionInstructions: Collect whole blood or bone marrow in EDTA.
assayLabRecords.rejectionCriteria: Serum, plasma, extracted DNA, CSF, FFPE tissue, ambient whole blood, frozen whole blood or bone marrow, non-EDTA anticoagulants, severely hemolyzed or clotted specimens.
assayLabRecords.reflexLogic: For uncertain diagnoses or unknown fusion forms, ARUP recommends ordering the diagnostic qualitative reflex assay (3005839) instead.
assayLabRecords.limitations: Intended for therapeutic monitoring rather than initial diagnostic characterization when fusion form is unknown.
assayLabRecords.interferences: RNA degradation can limit acceptable transit time.
assayLabRecords.notes: ARUP states the assay is designed to meet current NCCN guidance for molecular monitoring.

sourceLinks.note: Primary source for ordering recommendation and specimen handling.

assayLabRecords.recordTitle: ARUP Factor V Leiden (F5) R506Q Mutation
assayLabRecords.container: Lavender (EDTA), pink (K2EDTA), or yellow (ACD solution A or B)
assayLabRecords.handling: Counseling and informed consent are recommended for genetic testing.
assayLabRecords.stability: Room temperature: 3 days; Refrigerated: 1 week; Frozen: 1 month
assayLabRecords.useOrClinicalSignificance: Order for individuals at risk for venous thromboembolism when results will impact clinical management.
assayLabRecords.rejectionCriteria: Plasma or serum; sodium heparin tubes; frozen specimens in glass collection tubes.
assayLabRecords.includes: R506Q factor V Leiden mutation analysis
assayLabRecords.limitations: Not recommended for nonsymptomatic patients under 18 years of age.
assayLabRecords.notes: ARUP lists counseling and informed consent recommendations for genetic testing.

sourceLinks.label: ARUP Factor V Leiden overview
sourceLinks.note: Primary source for specimen, methodology, and LOINC.

assayLabRecords.recordTitle: Mayo Factor V Leiden (R506Q) Mutation, Blood
assayLabRecords.container: Preferred: Lavender top (EDTA); acceptable: yellow top (ACD solution B), light-blue top (sodium citrate)
assayLabRecords.handling: Send specimen in original tube. Do not aliquot.
assayLabRecords.useOrClinicalSignificance: DNA-based testing for the factor V Leiden variant used in thrombophilia evaluation.
assayLabRecords.patientPreparation: A previous bone marrow transplant from an allogenic donor will interfere with testing.
assayLabRecords.collectionInstructions: Invert several times to mix blood. Send specimen in original tube.
assayLabRecords.notes: Mayo exposes specimen requirements and LOINC metadata directly on the overview page.

sourceLinks.label: Mayo Factor V Leiden overview
sourceLinks.note: Primary source for specimen requirements and LOINC metadata.

assayLabRecords.recordTitle: Mayo TPMT and NUDT15 Genotype, Varies
assayLabRecords.testName: Thiopurine Methyltransferase (TPMT) and Nudix Hydrolase (NUDT15) Genotyping, Varies
assayLabRecords.useOrClinicalSignificance: Consider before initiating therapy with thiopurine drugs to better predict toxicity risk.
assayLabRecords.rejectionCriteria: All specimens will be evaluated at Mayo Clinic Laboratories for test suitability.
assayLabRecords.includes: TPMT genotype, TPMT phenotype, NUDT15 genotype, NUDT15 phenotype, and interpretation
assayLabRecords.reflexLogic: If genotype results do not match clinical findings, Mayo recommends considering TPMT enzyme activity testing.
assayLabRecords.limitations: This test will not detect all TPMT or NUDT15 variants and does not exclude toxicity risk from other factors.
assayLabRecords.interferences: Transfused donor DNA or allogeneic transplant can affect genotype interpretation.
assayLabRecords.notes: Mayo states integration of TPMT and NUDT15 may improve prediction of thiopurine-related toxicity across diverse populations.

sourceLinks.note: Primary source for gene coverage, cautions, and LOINC data.

sourceLinks.note: Supporting workflow reference for thiopurine management.

synonyms: Erlotinib Responsiveness in NSCLC, EGFR Mutation Analysis
Gefitinib Responsiveness in NSCLC, EGFR Mutation Analysis
assayLabRecords.specimenType: Formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue block or slides from NSCLC
assayLabRecords.specimenVolume: Five unstained slides and one matching H&E-stained slide at 10 uM or FFPE tissue block
assayLabRecords.minimumVolume: Two unstained slides and one matching H&E-stained slide at 10 uM
assayLabRecords.handling: Provide a copy of the pathology report.
assayLabRecords.useOrClinicalSignificance: In NSCLC, many EGFR mutations are associated with responsiveness to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy, while others are associated with resistance.
assayLabRecords.rejectionCriteria: Tumor block containing insufficient tumor; tissue or tumor fixed in a heavy metal fixative; broken or stained slides
assayLabRecords.limitations: No-mutation-detected results may still miss mutations not detected by the assay. Sensitivity depends on specimen integrity and tumor DNA content.
assayLabRecords.notes: Labcorp explicitly notes that T790M and exon 20 insertions are associated with resistance to EGFR TKI therapy.

sourceLinks.label: Labcorp EGFR mutation analysis
sourceLinks.note: Primary source for test details, specimen requirements, and turnaround time.

assayLabRecords.recordTitle: ARUP BCR-ABL1 Mutation Analysis for TKI Resistance by NGS
assayLabRecords.testName: BCR-ABL1 Mutation Analysis for Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor Resistance by Next Generation Sequencing
assayLabRecords.specimenVolume: Whole blood: 10 mL; bone marrow: 3 mL
assayLabRecords.minimumVolume: Whole blood: 2 mL; bone marrow: 1 mL
assayLabRecords.handling: Refrigerate. Separate specimens must be submitted when multiple tests are ordered.
assayLabRecords.useOrClinicalSignificance: Determine if a variant is present that would interfere with response to TKI therapy in Philadelphia chromosome positive leukemia.
assayLabRecords.collectionInstructions: Order only for patients with an established diagnosis of a BCR-ABL1-positive leukemia.
assayLabRecords.rejectionCriteria: Heparinized blood or bone marrow, serum, plasma, FFPE tissue, clotted or hemolyzed specimens, or specimens in non-EDTA anticoagulants.
assayLabRecords.reflexLogic: For initial BCR-ABL1 testing, ARUP directs users to the diagnostic qualitative assay with reflex to p190 or p210 quantitative assays (3005839).
assayLabRecords.limitations: This test is intended after a BCR-ABL1-positive diagnosis is already established.
assayLabRecords.notes: ARUP specifically identifies T315I among common detectable mutations.

sourceLinks.label: ARUP BCR-ABL1 resistance NGS overview
sourceLinks.note: Primary source for specimen requirements and resistance use case.

assayLabRecords.recordTitle: Mayo BCR/ABL1 Kinase Domain Mutation Screen, Sanger Sequencing
assayLabRecords.testName: BCR/ABL1, Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor Resistance, Kinase Domain Mutation Screen, Sanger Sequencing, Varies
assayLabRecords.handling: Specimens should be shipped as quickly as possible.
assayLabRecords.stability: Ambient specimens over 3 days old and refrigerated specimens over 5 days old are unacceptable.
assayLabRecords.methodology: Reverse transcription PCR followed by nested PCR and Sanger sequencing
assayLabRecords.useOrClinicalSignificance: Preferred initial test to identify acquired BCR::ABL1 mutations associated with TKI resistance in CML or Ph-positive B-ALL.
assayLabRecords.rejectionCriteria: If no fusion type is identified by qualitative testing, the assay is canceled.
assayLabRecords.includes: Kinase domain mutation screen and interpretive report
assayLabRecords.reflexLogic: If fusion type is not provided, a qualitative diagnostic assay for BCR::ABL1 is performed at additional charge.
assayLabRecords.limitations: Negative results do not exclude rare or poorly characterized mutations. Sensitivity declines at low transcript levels.
assayLabRecords.interferences: Low BCR::ABL1 transcript levels may be insufficient for successful amplification. Heparin cannot be used due to PCR inhibition.
assayLabRecords.notes: Mayo notes a general quantitative threshold above 0.1% BCR::ABL1/ABL1 is typically needed for successful mutation analysis.
